By using BODMAS RULE

After interchanging the number in given equation the equation is as follows : 15 × 24 + 40 – 7 ÷ 8 = 124

⇒ 15 × 24 + 40 – __**7 ÷ 8**__ = 124

⇒ __**15 × 24**__ + 40 – 0.875 = 124

⇒ __**360**____** + 40**__ – 0.875 = 124

⇒ __**7**____** × 15**__ + 40 – 3 = 124

​⇒ __**145 – 0.33**__ = 124

⇒ __**105 + 24**__ – 5 = 124

**LHS = RHS**

questions.question: Which finance minister of Mughal emperor Akbar introduced the system of taxation called 'Dahsala'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Raja Todar Mal.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• ​__Raja Todar Mal was the finance minister of the Mughal emperor Akbar. 
 
• He introduced the Dahsala system of taxation in **1580 AD. **
 
• This system was based on the average production of different crops over the past 10 years. 
 
• The state's share was one-third of the average produce. 
 
• The Dahsala system was adopted in most of the provinces of the Mughal Empire, **except for the ones that were predominantly Muslim.**
 
• The Dahsala system was a **more efficient and equitable system of taxation** than the previous systems. 
 
• It helped to ensure that the state received a fair share of the revenue, while also protecting the interests of the farmers. 
 
• The Dahsala system was also one of the factors that **contributed to the economic prosperity** of the Mughal empire during Akbar's reign.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• Raja Todar Mal divided all cultivable land into four categories:

 

 
• Polaj__: It was the best land cultivated every year.
 
• __Parauti__: It was the land of the second category which was left uncultivated for one year or two so that it could recover its fertility.
 
• __Chachar__: It was left uncultivated for three to four years in order to make it cultivable.
 
• __**Banjar:**__ Land that was not fit for agriculture and was mostly left uncultivated for a long time.

questions.question: The arteries divide into smaller vessels. On reaching the tissues, they divide further into extremely thin tubes called:
questions.solution:

__
 
• The arteries divide into smaller vessels. On reaching the tissues, they divide further into extremely thin tubes called **capillaries**.
 
• Capillaries are delicate blood vessels that exist throughout your body.
 
• They transport** blood, nutrients and oxygen **to cells in your organs and body systems.
 
• Capillaries are the** smallest blood vessels in your vascular system.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **An arteriole** is a very small blood vessel that branches off from your artery and carries blood away from your heart to your tissues and organs.

 
 
• Arterioles are small arteries that link up to capillaries, which are smaller yet.
 
 
 
• **Venules **are the smallest veins and receive blood from capillaries.
 
 
• They also play a role in the exchange of oxygen and nutrients for water products.
 
 
 
• **Veins** are blood vessels located throughout your body that collect oxygen-poor blood and return it to your heart.
 
 
• Veins are part of your circulatory system.

questions.question: A certain number of sweets can be equally distributed among 10, 20 and 25 children. But if there are 27 children and they are given equal number of sweets, 3 sweets are left. What is the minimum number of such sweets?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

LCM of 10, 20, and 25 is 100, so the total sweets must be a multiple of 100.

We check multiples of 100 for the condition: (Number ÷ 27) leaving a remainder of 3.

100 ÷ 27 → Remainder is 19.

200 ÷ 27 → Remainder is 11.

300 ÷ 27 → Remainder is 3 (since 300 = 27 × 11 + 3).

**∴ The correct answer is 300 sweets.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The number of sweets is completely divisible by 10, 20, and 25.

When divided among 27 children, 3 sweets are left.

**Concept Used:**

Number = LCM(a, b, c) × k

Dividend = Divisor × Quotient + Remainder

**Calculations:**

⇒ LCM of 10, 20, and 25 = 100

⇒ Let the required minimum number of sweets be 100k, where k is a positive integer (1, 2, 3...).

⇒ According to the second condition, 100k ÷ 27 leaves a remainder of 3.

⇒ This can be expressed as: 100k = 27q + 3

⇒ Since 100 = 27 × 3 + 19, we can simplify the expression by checking only the remainder part: 19k ÷ 27.

⇒ For k = 1: 19(1) ÷ 27 → Remainder is 19

⇒ For k = 2: 19(2) = 38 → 38 ÷ 27 → Remainder is 11

⇒ For k = 3: 19(3) = 57 → 57 ÷ 27 → Remainder is 3 (since 57 = 27 × 2 + 3)

⇒ Thus, the smallest integer value for k is 3.

⇒ Minimum number of sweets = 100 × 3 = 300

**∴ The correct answer is 300 sweets.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and HCF Relationship

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their LCM and HCF: A × B = LCM × HCF.

Remainder Theorem

Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder. This is the core equation used for solving divisibility and remainder problems.

Common Remainder Rule

The smallest number which when divided by x, y, and z leaves a common remainder r in each case is represented as: LCM(x, y, z) + r.
</p

**∴ The correct answer is 12 coins.**
